item.title: Ad-conditions for higher-order recurrences: Dunkl and matrix-valued settings
item.description: arXiv:2611.00219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The ad-conditions of Duistermaat and Gr\"unbaum characterize bispectrality for a pair of differential operators. M.~Reach observed that a sequence of functions which is simultaneously an eigenfunction of a second-order differential operator and satisfies a recurrence relation of arbitrary order must satisfy a different kind of ad-conditions. We prove that the Reach ad-conditions are also sufficient, by an argument which is purely algebraic. This motivated us to explore ad-conditions in two new directions: to Dunkl differential-difference operators, where the coefficients of the ad-condition become elements of the Dunkl algebra and the reflection enters as a coefficient, and to matrix-valued orthogonal polynomials, where we exhibit ad-conditions for several families of exceptional matrix-valued polynomials satisfying five- and seven-term recurrence relations.
item.dc:creator: I. Bono Parisi, F. A. Gr\"unbaum, I. Zurri\'an

item.title: Second order Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle for solenoidal fields: sharp constants, optimizers and sharp stability
item.description:
arXiv:2611.00362v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The second order Heisenberg Uncertainty Principle of Cazacu, Flynn and Lam is the uncertainty principle for the gradient of a function. Motivated by the question of Maz'ya on the uncertainty principle for divergence-free vector fields, solved by Cazacu, Flynn and Lam for $N=2$ and by Hamamoto for $N\ge3$, we study the second order principle for divergence-free fields $\mathbf{U}$ on $\mathbb{R}^N$. We prove that $\int|\Delta\mathbf{U}|^2dx\int|x|^2|
abla\mathbf{U}|^2dx\ge C_N^2(\int|
abla\mathbf{U}|^2dx)^2$, where $C_N=1+ rac12\sqrt{N^2+8}$ for $N\ge3$ and $C_2=1+\sqrt2$. For the velocity of an incompressible flow, $\int|
abla\mathbf{U}|^2$ and $\int|\Delta\mathbf{U}|^2$ are, up to constant factors, the enstrophy and the palinstrophy, so the inequality bounds the palinstrophy from below in terms of the enstrophy and the spatial spread of the velocity gradient. The constant $C_N$ is sharp and larger than the constant $ rac{N+2}{2}$ for general fields, and all the optimizers are explicit fields with Kummer function profiles. We also obtain the sharp constants on the poloidal and the toroidal fields of each degree. Then we prove the sharp stability of the inequality. In sum form, the deficit controls a chain of squared distances to explicit families of poloidal and toroidal fields, with all the constants sharp. In product form, we find the sharp stability constant in all dimensions. For $N\ge4$ it is $ rac12(\sqrt{N^2+4N-4}-\sqrt{N^2+8})$, and it is attained by swirling flows, the toroidal fields of degree one. On the Fourier side, the sixth order poloidal problem becomes a first order Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequality for radial functions, and its stability follows from weighted Poincar'e inequalities with Gaussian type measures.
item.dc:creator: Anh Xuan Do, Anh Tuan Duong, Nguyen Lam, Guozhen Lu, Van Hoang Nguyen

item.title: On the properties of the potential and the spherical harmonic expansions for general planets
item.description: arXiv:2611.00389v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The convergence of spherical harmonic expansions (SHEs) of gravitational potentials below the Brillouin sphere has been a long-standing problem in potential theory and geodesy. In previous work, some of the present authors gave a necessary and sufficient condition for convergence along a fixed ray, formulated in terms of analyticity of a longitudinal average of the balayage density. In the present paper, we extend these results to arbitrary physical solid planets, assuming only that the planet is a compact subset of $\mathbb R^3$ and that its density belongs to $L^\infty$. We establish sharp regularity properties of the gravitational potential at the Brillouin sphere. The potential and its first derivative extend continuously to the sphere, the first derivative is locally H\"older continuous with exponent $1/2$, and the second derivative satisfies the optimal bound $V''(z)=O\bigl(\operatorname{dist}(z,\partial\mathbb D)^{-1/2}\bigr)$ under nontangential approach from the exterior. We also obtain sharp estimates for the spherical harmonic coefficients: $a_\ell=O(\ell^{-3/2}).$ If, for almost every latitude, the Brillouin sphere is a one-sided Lebesgue point from the interior of the longitudinally averaged density, then $a_\ell=o(\ell^{-3/2}).$ Both estimates are optimal. We explicitly recover the balayage density on the Brillouin sphere from the exterior gravitational potential, and its circular averages from the potential along a single radial line. Finally, we give a physical characterization of convergence of the SHE below the Brillouin sphere. If the SHE converges at such a point, then, after truncating the planet at any suitable intermediate radius, the gravitational potential of the removed outer part is completely determined by that of the remaining truncated planet. This provides a direct interpretation of the strong constraint imposed by convergence below the Brillouin sphere.
item.dc:creator: Ovidiu Costin, Rodica D. Costin, Marjorie K. Drake, Gerald V. Dunne, Crichton Ogle

item.title: Bilateral Christoffel-Geronimus-Uvarov formulas for mixed-type orthogonality on algebraic supports
item.description: arXiv:2611.00457v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Christoffel-type determinant formulas construct both normalized polynomial families and their reproducing kernel for mixed-type orthogonality in several variables after independent rational matrix transformations on the two arguments. The pairing may have a rectangular matrix of functionals, with separate degree bounds on each component, and may be supported on an algebraic variety. The reduced matrices are calculated from the original biorthogonal polynomials, rational moments, polynomial division and the masses left free by division; their nonvanishing determinants characterize existence and uniqueness. For measure pairings the rational data are expressed by Cauchy and multivariate Fantappie transforms. Exact dimension counts incorporate the four matrix factors and the relations of the support. For normal degree-ordered original families and fixed factors, when the component degrees on each side differ by a bounded amount and the normalization dimension grows at most like one degree layer, the resulting orders are bounded on curves and grow at most linearly on surfaces. For pairings allowing scalar factors to move between arguments, called balanced pairings, an exact obstruction determines whether a bilateral mass decomposes into unilateral masses when the denominators act injectively. Residue duality provides coordinates for division and mass quotients on integral curves, including singular points, and on the finite surface quotients specified here. Explicit singular-curve families retain nondegenerate residue pairings as denominator zeros coalesce. Positive congruences admit a further reduction by orthogonal projection, while balanced pairings give simultaneous intertwining identities for all coordinate multiplication matrices.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Ma\~nas

item.title: Conjectures of Bernstein and Erd\H{o}s for weighted Lagrange interpolation with Hermite weight
item.description: arXiv:2611.00809v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The classical Bernstein and Erd\H{o}s Conjectures for algebraic Lagrange interpolation on a finite interval were settled in two consecutive papers by Kilgore and by de Boor and Pinkus in 1978. Extending these results to weighted interpolation on unbounded intervals has proved to be more difficult. In a previous work, we established the Bernstein and Erd\H os Conjectures, together with the ``modified'' de Boor--Pinkus intertwining theorem, for weighted Lagrange interpolation on the half-line with exponential weights. Here we continue this line of research by considering the Hermite weight on the whole real line. Our main result is the Hermite-weighted analogue of the Bernstein and Erd\H{o}s conjectures together with the appropriate version of the de Boor--Pinkus intertwining theorem. A key ingredient in the classical proofs is the nonsingularity of certain derivative matrices associated with the local maxima of the Lebesgue function. This property already breaks down in the exponentially weighted setting, although the resulting difficulties can still be resolved. In the Hermite-weighted setting, however, the situation becomes more intricate, requiring a substantial refinement of the previous approach.
item.dc:creator: B\'ela Nagy, Patr\'icia Szokol, Szil\'ard Gy. R\'ev\'esz

item.title: The Two-Point Inequality for $p>q$
item.description: arXiv:2611.00835v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $1<q<p<\infty$ we study the $L^p\to L^q$ contractivity of the two-point operator $T_\omega(a+bx)=a+\omega bx$ with a complex parameter $\omega$, extending the Weissler two-point condition, usually discussed in the range $1<p\le q<\infty$, to the reversed order of exponents. For $1<q<p<2$ we prove that the second-order necessary condition $|(p-2)-(q-2)\omega^2|\le p-q|\omega|^2$, obtained near $(a,b)=(1,0)$, is also sufficient; by duality the same description applies to $2<q<p<\infty$. The proof uses the method of characteristic flows. In addition, for $q\le2\le p$ the contractivity follows directly from $L^2$ contraction.
item.dc:creator: Di Wu

item.title: Some Characterisations of the Strichartz Fourier Transform on the Heisenberg Group
item.description: arXiv:2611.01128v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Recently, Thangavelu introduced a scalar-valued Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group, built from the joint spectral theory of the sublaplacian and the central vector field. Around the same time, Krukowski characterised the classical Fourier transform on various groups from a small number of structural properties, paired with a normalisation hypothesis. In this paper, we obtain analogous results for the Strichartz Fourier transform on the Heisenberg group. Here, the spectral property is formulated jointly for the sublaplacian and the central vector field, and the translation property is based on a twisted form of left translation. The joint spectral property, paired with the twisted translation property and a normalisation at a single explicit test function, characterises the Strichartz Fourier transform on each ray of the underlying spectral set, the Heisenberg fan. The twisted translation property alone, paired with a Dirac delta property, already suffices. We also characterise the radial kernel of the transform on each ray by a Laguerre-type differential equation.
item.dc:creator: R. Lakshmi Lavanya

item.title: Bochner-Riesz means for Laguerre expansions
item.description: arXiv:2611.01221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate the $L^p$ norm convergence of Bochner-Riesz means $S_R^\delta f$, $f \in L^p(\mathbb{R}^+,d\mu_\beta)$ associated to Laguerre expansions of type $\beta \geq -1/2$. For any given $1 < p < \infty$ and $\beta > -1/2$, we provide a complete characterisation of the order $\delta$ for which these means are uniformly bounded on $L^p$ spaces. A particularly noteworthy phenomenon arises for $-1/3 <\beta <0$, where the admissible $(p, \delta)$ region differs substantially from those for $ -1/2 \leq \beta \leq -1/3$ or $\beta \geq 0$. Interestingly, the convergence for $-1/3 < \beta <0$ is an interaction between the ranges $ -1/2 \leq \beta \leq -1/3$ and $\beta \geq 0$.
item.dc:creator: Himani Sharma, Adam Sikora, Sundaram Thangavelu

item.title: The sharp Stein-Tomas inequality on the circle
item.description: arXiv:2611.01318v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that constant functions are global maximizers for the endpoint Stein--Tomas inequality on $\mathbb{S}^1$, thereby determining its sharp constant. By the known characterization of the phases of maximizers, every nonzero maximizer then has the form $f(\omega)=c e^{ix_0\cdot\omega}$, where $c\in\mathbb{C}\setminus\{0\}$ and $x_0\in\mathbb{R}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Yaojun Wang

item.title: Perfectness of partial Christoffel transforms of Nikishin systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.01395v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study multiple orthogonal polynomial systems obtained from a Nikishin system of two measures by applying a Christoffel transform to one of the measures at a point $x=x_0$. We show that if $x_0$ separates the supports of the generating measures, then the modified systems remain perfect. As an application, we prove that the type I multiple orthogonal polynomials of a Nikishin system have no zeros in the gap between the supports of its generating measures.
item.dc:creator: Rostyslav Kozhan

item.title: The MZ-property for three-term differences
item.description: arXiv:2611.01406v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Marcinkiewicz--Zygmund property for finite differences. A difference \[ D(f,h)=\sum_{k=1}^n a_k f(b_kh) \] is said to have the MZ-property if, for every measurable function $f$, \[ D(f,h)=o(h) \quad\text{and}\quad f(h)=o(1) \] imply \[ f(h)=o(h). \] In this paper, we characterize all three-node differences \[ D(f,h)=af(qh)+bf(rh)+cf(sh) \] having the MZ-property. In particular, for irrational differences with distinct nodes, we obtain explicit necessary and sufficient conditions in terms of the coefficients $a,b,c$ and the nodes $q,r,s$. As an application, our results resolve an open problem concerning a second-order Riemann difference.
item.dc:creator: Hajrudin Fejzi\'c, Chris Freiling

item.title: The Marvelous Meixner Polynomials: Second Kind, First Class
item.description: arXiv:2611.01422v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Meixner's classification asks which exponential generating functions can generate orthogonal polynomials. We follow the continuous Meixner family from this question to its moments, measures, and continued fractions. A beta integral and a bilinear identity establish positivity and orthogonality; Carlitz's Bernoulli and Euler constructions reveal further connections. Turning the parameter into a variable leads to rational orthogonality and Wall's fraction. We derive its Nevanlinna measure and unite the two spectral directions in a joint law with Cauchy marginals. Even finite pencils produce couplings with these exact marginals. Laguerre limits explain the gamma law governing joint extremes. Along the way, Meixner's scientific life, combinatorics, tangent numbers, and even zeta values illuminate the same structure.
item.dc:creator: Olga Holtz

item.title: A log-concavity criterion for finite nonnegative linearization
item.description: arXiv:2611.01561v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In a 2005 survey, R. Szwarc asked for criteria, stated in the recurrence coefficients, for nonnegative linearization (property (P)) of finite orthogonal polynomial systems such as the Krawtchouk polynomials. For a finite three-term recurrence normalized to have row sums one, whose diagonal and downward coefficients have a constant nonnegative ratio, we prove that property (P) holds for every product, including products beyond the terminal degree, whenever the Newton coefficients of the profile $d_i=b_i+c_i$ are log-concave without internal zeros. The criterion contains the full positive Krawtchouk range and the dual $q$-Krawtchouk arrays, and through a quadratic decomposition of symmetric finite systems it covers Szwarc's quadratic system $Q_n$ in its sharp range $0<p_0\leq1/2$. As a limit to any such criterion, property (P) fails at coefficient distance $O((1-r^2)^N)$ from the Krawtchouk array of size $N$ with fixed ratio $c_i/d_i=r<1$. All theorems, corollaries and propositions are formalized in Lean 4.
item.dc:creator: Leslie P. Polzer

item.title: Percentile oscillations and the intrinsic square function
item.description: arXiv:2611.01687v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Wilson's intrinsic square function tests the input against all the cancellative functions of a given smoothness, at every location and scale. We show that it is dominated pointwise by a sparse square function, whose coefficients are the percentile oscillations of the input modulo polynomials, at every polynomial order below the smoothness plus one. These coefficients are local sizes, which nevertheless retain essentially all the cancellation: the weighted norms of the sparse square function are equivalent to smooth grand maximal norms, for all $0<p<\infty$ and $A_\infty$ weights, with explicit dependence on the weight. These are weighted Hardy norms in the range allowed by the smoothness. Consequences include potential bounds, and weighted Hardy space estimates with the sharp factor $[w]_{A_\infty}^{1/2}$. For the derivatives of Calder\'on--Zygmund operators, we characterize the corresponding square function estimates by testing conditions on the polynomial symbols of their wavelet resolution. In the quadratic setting, the factor $[w]_{A_\infty}^{1/2}$ detects a transition from $\mathrm{BMO}$ testing conditions to vanishing symbols.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Di Plinio

item.title: On Variational Inequalities for Averages over Hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper establishes sharp variational estimates for families of averaging operators over smooth hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$. For a hypersurface with $k$ non-zero principal curvatures at a given point, we prove that the $r$-variation operator $V_r(A_t f : t>0)$ is bounded on $L^p$ for all exponents satisfying $(k+1)/k < p < r(k+1)$, with operator norm depending explicitly on a translation parameter $D$. In the special case $k=n$ (i.e., non-vanishing Gaussian curvature), we show that the range $p<r(n+1)$ is optimal, thereby recovering and extending classical results for the sphere. Furthermore, for convex hypersurfaces of finite type (in the sense of Iosevich-Sawyer), we obtain variational bounds in the range $p_0 < p < 2r$, where $p_0$ is the contact index of the associated hypersurface. The proofs combine long-short variational decompositions, stationary phase analysis, vector-valued singular integrals, and local smoothing estimates for Fourier integral operators. These results unify and generalize earlier work on maximal functions and variational inequalities for averages over hypersurfaces.
item.dc:creator: Xudong Nie, Panwang Wang

item.title: Another Application of the Alternating Map: Time-and-Band Limiting
item.description: arXiv:2611.01839v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use Castillo's dual formulation of classicality for the alternating map to reduce polynomial time-and-band limiting to two scalar problems. The reconstruction preserves polynomial cutoffs, multipliers and concentration forms. It recovers the symmetric Dunkl constructions of Castro and Gr\"unbaum and applies to continuous and discrete inputs. Scalar recurrences avoid moment factorizations; positive integrals and residual bounds control the accuracy of the concentration values.
item.dc:creator: Lucas Tertuliano da Silva

item.title: The signed error-sum function of tent-map expansions
item.description: arXiv:2611.01955v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we study the signed error-sum function of tent map base series introduced by Dai and Tang in 2011. We show that the function is discontinuous at every dyadic rational in the open unit interval, although it was asserted to be continuous. We determine its values at these points and analyze its range, differentiability, and variation. We also obtain sharp covering estimates for its graph and calculate the Hausdorff, box-counting, and covering dimensions of the graph, which are $1$, $1$, and $0$, respectively. Moreover, we show that the signed error sum agrees with L\'evy's function away from dyadic rationals and that the unsigned error sum is the Takagi function.
item.dc:creator: Min Woong Ahn

item.title: The local-to-global minimum problem of Calvert and Vamanamurthy: a quartic counterexample in three variables and the cubic case in all dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.02068v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In 1980 Calvert and Vamanamurthy asked whether a polynomial whose only critical point is a local minimum must attain its global minimum there. They gave counterexamples of every degree at least five in two or more variables and settled cubics in two and three variables and quartics in two variables, leaving open quartics in three or more variables and cubics in four or more variables. We resolve both remaining cases. First, we give an explicit quartic in three variables whose unique critical point is a nondegenerate strict local minimum, although the polynomial is unbounded below; the example extends to every dimension at least three, and its critical locus is a single point even over the complex numbers. Second, we prove that in every dimension a polynomial of exact degree three with a local minimum has another critical point, so that the cubic case holds vacuously; the proof is elementary and avoids the topological degree arguments used previously in two and three variables. Together with the results of Calvert and Vamanamurthy, this gives the complete classification of the local-to-global property by degree and dimension.
item.dc:creator: Hugo Adu\'en

item.title: On a hybrid trilinear Hilbert transform
item.description: arXiv:2611.02167v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper we study the boundedness properties of a \emph{hybrid} trilinear Hilbert transform characterized by a \emph{dual regime} which simultaneously exhibits 1) \emph{resonant} (zero curvature) features, \emph{i.e.}, modulation invariance properties, and 2) \emph{non-resonant} (non-zero curvature) features. Specifically, given $a\in(0,\infty)\setminus \{1,2\}$ and $\vec{\lambda}:=(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3,\lambda_4)\in (\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\})^4$ with $\lambda_1\neq \lambda_2$ and $\lambda_3\neq \lambda_4$, we provide wide-range $L^p$ bounds for the trilinear operator $$ HTHT^a_{\vec{\lambda}} (f_1,f_2,f_3)(x):= p.v. \int_{\mathbb R} f_1(x-\lambda_1 t)\,f_2(x-\lambda_2 t-\lambda_3 t^a)\,f_3(x-\lambda_4 t^a)\,\frac{dt}{t},\quad x \in \mathbb{R}\,.$$ By combining variable multiresolution, multiscale wave-packet analysis, and Rank II LGC method, our present work establishes a common framework where the diverse methodologies of all of the following naturally converge: i) the maximal truncated bilinear Hilbert transform, ii) the Biest operator, iii) the hybrid bilinear Hilbert-Carleson operator, and iv) the non-resonant (curved) trilinear Hilbert transform. Ultimately, this work reveals that the hybrid trilinear transform sits on a critical intermediate scale between the purely non-resonant case and the purely resonant regime -- the latter remaining a challenging, major (open) problem in harmonic analysis.
item.dc:creator: Cristina Benea, Fr\'ed\'eric Bernicot, Victor Lie

item.title: Separating the Polar of Sets of Uniqueness from the Polars of All $H^{(d)}$-Sets
item.description: arXiv:2611.02241v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a perfect set of uniqueness on the circle carrying a continuous probability measure which annihilates every $H^{(d)}$-set, simultaneously for all finite dimensions d. This gives a strict inclusion between the polar of the compact sets of uniqueness and the polar of the union of the classes $H^{(d)}$, answering a question raised in earlier work on these polars. The construction uses random binary increments of size comparable to the reciprocal of a product of square roots. A Gaussian sampling estimate gives a uniform Fourier-tail bound for all pseudomeasures supported by the resulting set, and also bounded atomic approximation and spectral synthesis. A separate energy estimate, stable under deletion of a small number of increments, yields full support for every limiting quasi-independent image of every positive measure absolutely continuous with respect to the constructed measure.
item.dc:creator: V\'aclav Vlas\'ak

item.title: Pointwise Ergodic Theorems Along $\lfloor p^c\rfloor$ for Every $c>1$
item.description: arXiv:2611.02465v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $c>1$ be noninteger, and let $\Lambda$ denote the von Mangoldt function. The averages \[ A_N^{c} f(x):=\frac1N\sum_{n=1}^{N} \Lambda(n)f\bigl(T^{\lfloor n^c\rfloor}x\bigr) \] satisfy the variational estimate \[ \bigl\|\mathcal{V}^r(A_N^{c} f:N\in\mathbb{N})\bigr\|_{L^p(X)} \lesssim_{c,p,r}\|f\|_{L^p(X)} \] for every $1<p<\infty$ and $r>2$, on every $\sigma$-finite measure-preserving system. In particular, the normalized averages along fractional powers of primes converge almost everywhere. The main arithmetic ingredient is a uniform bound on the correlations of $\Lambda-1$ with fractional-power exponential phases, yielding arbitrarily large powers of logarithmic gain. We obtain this estimate through short-interval polynomial approximation of the fractional phase and higher-order discorrelation estimates. The same approach yields almost-everywhere convergence to for the M\"obius-weighted averages along $\left( \lfloor n^c \rfloor \right)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ throughout $1<p<\infty$.
item.dc:creator: Anastasios Fragkos

item.title: Bilinear maximal functions associated with some degenerate surfaces on the Heisenberg group
item.description: arXiv:2611.02745v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Motivated by the works of Lee--Shuin and Borges--Foster on the Euclidean space, in this article we consider bilinear averages on the Heisenberg group $\mathbb{H}^n$ corresponding to some degenerate surfaces associated with the Kor\'anyi norm as well as Nevo--Thangavelu type averaging structures, and study the boundedness of the their full and lacunary maximal functions on various $L^{p}(\mathbb{H}^n) \times L^{q}(\mathbb{H}^n)$ spaces, for $n \geq 2$. For the full maximal functions, we obtain optimal range except possibly at the end points.
item.dc:creator: Sayan Bagchi, Rahul Garg, Surya Kanta Rana

item.title: The critical line for modulation invariant bilinear multipliers
item.description: arXiv:2611.02768v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the bilinear multipliers with symbols singular along a nondegenerate line, in the class of Muscalu, Tao and Thiele, map $L^{p_1}(\mathbb R)\times L^{p_2}(\mathbb R)$ into $L^{2/3,\infty}(\mathbb R)$ on the whole critical line \[ \frac1{p_1}+\frac1{p_2}=\frac32,\qquad 1<p_1,p_2<2 . \] This is sharp, as no estimate into $L^{p,\infty}$ with $p<\frac23$ holds uniformly over the class. Moreover, the generalized restricted weak type estimates of the class extend, without logarithmic loss, to the open short sides of the hexagon of exponents. For the bilinear Hilbert transforms, this confirms a folklore conjecture recorded by Thiele and the author, and removes the doubly logarithmic term in their endpoint estimates. The main step is an improvement over the multi-frequency Calder\'on--Zygmund decompositions already present in the literature. The bad part of this version has vanishing moments of order one at the top frequencies of the trees close to each Whitney interval, and vanishing moments of logarithmic order at the frequency bins where the tops of distant trees accumulate.
item.dc:creator: Francesco Di Plinio

item.title: On some positivity properties of the Riemann $\Xi$ function
item.description: arXiv:2611.02944v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove strict log-concavity of the positive functions $\Theta$ and $\Lambda$ with one-sided and bilateral Laplace transforms $1/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)$ and $1/\Xi$, respectively, where $\Xi(z)=\xi(\tfrac12+iz)$. For either function, log-concavity is the P\'olya frequency property of order two (PF$_2$). Without assuming the Riemann hypothesis (RH), but using its published verification up to height about $3\cdot10^{12}$, we further prove that both densities are PF$_{k_*}$ for $k_*=1\,810\,540\,931\,075$. The proof views $\Theta$ as a small signed perturbation of a density that is PF of every order, with an error bound independent of the order, so the numerical check reduces to scalar inequalities. Since $\Lambda$ is a Gaussian mixture of $\Theta$, it inherits the same order. Conversely, a pole obstruction shows that if either density is PF$_k$, then every zeta zero lower than the $(k+2)$-nd lies on the critical line. Finally, we prove that if RH holds up to height $T>\tfrac12$, then $\Xi$ satisfies the generalized Laguerre inequalities $L_n[\Xi](x)\ge0$ of every order $n$ for $|x|\le T-\tfrac12$, extending the case $n=1$ of Csordas, Ruttan and Varga (1991).
item.dc:creator: Suvrit Sra

item.title: Any uniformly rectifiable set is contained in a set with Poincar\'e inequality
item.description: arXiv:2611.03153v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that any uniformly $d$-rectifiable subset of $\mathbb{R}^n$ is contained in an Ahlfors $d$-regular set in $\mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ which supports a $(1,1)$-Poincar\'e inequality. This provides a natural converse to a recent result of Azzam.
item.dc:creator: Matthew Hyde, Michele Villa, Ivan Yuri Violo

item.title: Characterization of the group Fourier transform of Hilbert space Valued functions
item.description: arXiv:2611.03267v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A remarkable theorem of S. Alesker, S. Artstein-Avidan, and V. Milman characterizes the Fourier transform on $\mathbb{R}^n$ as, in essence, the unique transformation on the space of tempered distributions that exchanges convolution with pointwise multiplication. In this paper, we extend this perspective to the setting of the Heisenberg group $\He$, focusing on functions taking values in a separable Hilbert space $\Hi$. We establish a characterization of the group Fourier transform on $\He$ in terms of convolution. More precisely, we characterize the group Fourier transform on $L^1(\He,\Hi)$ and $L^2(\He,\Hi)$. In addition, we obtain a similar characterization for the group Fourier transform of $\Hi$-valued Schwartz class functions on the Heisenberg group.
item.dc:creator: Satyajyoti Achar, Md Hasan Ali Biswas, Ramesh Manna

item.title: Hyperplane Furstenberg Sets in Higher Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2611.03504v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The hyperplane Furstenberg problem asks how small the Hausdorff dimension of $E\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ can be when a $t$-dimensional family of affine $(n-1)$-dimensional hyperplanes meets $E$ in sets of dimension at least $s$. For $0<s\le n-1$ and $0<t\le n$, we prove the sharp bound in $\mathbb{R}^n$ $\dim_{\mathrm{H}}E\ge\mathbf{F}(s,t;n,n-1)$, where $\mathbf{F}$ is Gan's Furstenberg index proposed in prime fields. We also construct examples attaining this bound for all parameters. Our main reduction theorem, Theorem 3.1, states that for $n\ge3$, $0<s\le n-2$, and $1<t\le n$, every weighted $(s,t)$ configuration $(E,H)$ at scale $\delta$ produces a dual weighted $(s,t-1)$ configuration $(P,\mathcal{T})$ inside a hyperplane $H_{y_0}\cong\mathbb{R}^{n-1}$. The reduction uses radial projection and energy estimates for Frostman measures. Iterating this reduction and applying the Cs\"ornyei--Stull incidence theorem yields the bound.
item.dc:creator: Peiqi Nie

item.title: Lecture note on Fourier decoupling theory and its applications
item.description: arXiv:2611.03549v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper is based on lecture notes taken and organized during the 17th Graduate Mathematics Intensive Training Program (Spring 2025), held at the Beijing International Center for Mathematical Research, in which Professor Shaoming Guo lectured on "An Introduction to Fourier Decoupling Theory." The main content includes an introduction to and proofs of $\ell^2$ decoupling inequality, together with its applications in number theory, harmonic analysis, and geometric measure theory. The writing follows Professor Guo's teaching style, proving theorems in an intuitive and heuristic manner; consequently, the text contains many figures to explain the ideas at hand, while also lacking some rigor. However, all of these geometric intuitions can be rigorously justified, albeit in a more complicated and technical way. The author hopes that readers will be able to understand, through these lecture notes, the geometric intuition hidden behind the cumbersome proofs, and thereby deepen their understanding of the relevant definitions and theorems. Rigorous proofs can be found in Professor Guo's forthcoming book, which interested readers may consult.
item.dc:creator: Yudong Liang

item.title: A Proof for Generalized Egalitarianism
item.description: arXiv:2610.40312v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This paper proves a rigidity theorem characterizing the Gini-type Lorenz-area ordering under general decision-theoretic constraints together with weak Lorenz dominance, thereby resolving the characterization problem pursued in this line of research on egalitarianism. This does not, of course, bring the broader inquiry to an end. In a certain sense, it may instead mark a step beyond the infancy of our attempt to connect social choice theory, welfare economics, and formal moral philosophy through a common mathematical language. The main proof strategy was originally obtained by the author's own hand, though 5.6sol and Astra could effortlessly reproduce it without any additional hint.
item.dc:creator: Wei ShuAng

item.title: Intersections of fractal sets with rectifiable curves
item.description: arXiv:2610.41510v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K \subset\mathbb{R}^d$, $d\ge2$, be a connected compact set and $\phi(t)=tL(t)$ be a gauge function with $L$ non-increasing. We study intersections of $K$ with rectifiable curves and chord-arc curves. We show that if $\int_0^1\frac{dt}{\phi(t)}<\infty$, then there exists a rectifiable curve $\gamma\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ such that $\mathcal{H}^\phi(K \cap\gamma)>0$. Moreover, for every $0<s<1$, there exists a chord-arc curve $\gamma$ such that $\textrm{H$.$dim}(K \cap\gamma)\ge s$. Conversely, we show that if $K$ is uniformly porous on lines and $\int_0^1\frac{dt}{\phi(t)}=\infty$, then $\mathcal{H}^\phi(K \cap\gamma)=0$ for every rectifiable curve $\gamma$ and $\textrm{H$.$dim}(K \cap\gamma)<1$ for every chord-arc curve $\gamma$.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Ivrii, Truong Vu

item.title: Painlev\'e VI superintegrability and Heun-Racah algebras
item.description: arXiv:2611.00322v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the two fourth-order quantum superintegrable systems in the Euclidean plane that separate in polar coordinates and whose angular potentials are determined by the general four-parameter sixth Painlev\'e transcendent. One system has an oscillator radial term and the other an extended-Coulomb radial term. For both systems we give the fourth-order quantum integral explicitly, derive the cubic symmetry algebra and its Casimir, and construct a deformed-oscillator realization. At fixed energy the two algebras are specializations of the Heun--Racah algebra. Their structure functions contain the same quartic angular factor, determined by the Painlev\'e~VI parameters, while different radial factors distinguish oscillator and Coulomb dynamics. The Coulomb integral is obtained by transforming the Cartesian Hermitian symmetry at the operator level. The lower-order terms generated by the polar coordinate change are essential for commutation with the Hamiltonian. The two quantum systems are also related by the Levi-Civita transformation and coupling-constant metamorphosis, which gives a direct correspondence between their Painlev\'e parameters, algebras, Casimirs and representations. Earlier exceptional-Jacobi models arise at special rational parameter values, whereas the results here apply to the full four-parameter Painlev\'e~VI family. We also compare the quantum results with the corresponding classical Poisson algebras.
item.dc:creator: Ian Marquette, Sarah Post

item.title: A dual approach to $L^p$ estimates for orthogonal martingales satisfying the differential subordination
item.description: arXiv:2611.00932v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop a new dual approach, which can be used to establish sharp $L^p$ bounds for orthogonal differentially subordinate martingales. The method rests on the construction of a certain special function enjoying appropriate majorization properties and a novel differential condition.
item.dc:creator: Rodrigo Ba\~nuelos, Adam Os\k{e}kowski

item.title: Markov-driven self-similar measures and non-homogeneous slicing
item.description: arXiv:2611.00962v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce the concept of Markov-driven self-similar measures, a notion that simultaneously generalizes classical self-similar measures, self-conformal measures, dynamically driven self-similar measures and many random measures. This class is also closed under Cartesian products and linear projections. We initiate the study of this class of measures and investigate the $L^q$ dimension of Markov-driven self-similar measures under certain Diophantine conditions. As an application, we obtain the first Furstenberg slicing type results for intersections of Cantor sets in non-homogeneous settings.
item.dc:creator: Pablo Shmerkin, Shunsuke Usuki

item.title: On the Finite-Time Singularities of Point-Vortex Systems I: The Half-Plane
item.description: arXiv:2611.01014v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, the first in a series devoted to finite-time singularities of point-vortex systems in domains with boundaries, we establish the existence of finite-time interior collapse for three vortices in the upper half-plane $\mathbb{H}^+$. Our approach treats the boundary-induced interactions as a perturbation of the classical self-similar Gr\"{o}bli collapse in the full plane. Under suitable conditions on the vortex circulations and collapse profile, we prove the existence of a one-dimensional local strong stable manifold of the augmented rescaled system, which generates exact solutions in which three distinct vortices collapse simultaneously at any prescribed interior point $z^*\in\mathbb{H}^+$. Moreover, these solutions are asymptotically self-similar, with the characteristic square-root collapse rate $O(\sqrt{T-t})$.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Yang

item.title: Functions of $\boldsymbol{S}_p$-almost commuting unitary operators and contractions. An extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula
item.description: arXiv:2611.01149v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we study functions of pairs of unitary operators and pairs of contractions with commutators in the Schatten-von Neumann class $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. We obtain commutator estimates and prove that our functional calculus is multiplicative modulo $\boldsymbol{S}_p$. On the other hand, we show that our commutator estimates do not extend to the case $p>2$. We also obtain an extension of the Carey--Pincus trace formula. The main tool of this paper is a technique of triple operator integrals.
item.dc:creator: A. B. Aleksandrov, V. V. Peller

item.title: Coefficientwise Hankel-total positivity from a universal cumulant lifting
item.description: arXiv:2611.01172v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Using probabilistic methods, we establish universal cumulant lifting criteria for Stieltjes and Hamburger moment sequences. In the Stieltjes case, we characterize coefficientwise Hankel total positivity after convolution with every initial moment sequence by requiring each once-shifted cumulant sequence to be Stieltjes. We also prove equivalence with the numerical moment property at every nonnegative intensity. In the Hamburger case, we use twice-shifted cumulants to obtain coefficientwise-positive leading Hankel determinants, a degree bound, an explicit highest-degree component, and drift invariance. We work with formal series and require neither exponential moments nor moment determinacy. We establish composition, binomial-convolution, and substitution results, and apply them to implicit equations and autonomous differential equations, tree and forest families, and lognormal compound-Poisson moments in a unified approach. From known moment sequences, we obtain general coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive families containing the classical Bessel, Lah, and Laguerre polynomials. We not only give new proofs of coefficientwise Hankel-total positivity of many combinatorial polynomials, but also prove coefficientwise Hankel total positivity for the component polynomials of functional digraphs confirming a conjecture of Sokal and establish fixed-shape Schl\"afli--Gessel--Seo polynomials positivity supporting another conjecture of Sokal.
item.dc:creator: Bao-Xuan Zhu

item.title: A general framework for universal bounds on the analytic functional calculus
item.description: arXiv:2611.01503v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We establish a general principle for bounding the matrix-valued analytic functional calculus $F\mapsto F(T)$ of a Hilbert space operator $T$, independently of the matrix size. It rests on two properties of an auxiliary Hilbert space of holomorphic functions: the accretivity of its moment map at $T$ and a uniform bound for its multipliers. The mechanism of OpenAI's direct proof of the complete Crouzeix conjecture is the instance in which these properties come from the positivity of the double-layer potential and from norm estimates for Faber series of a convex domain. The main advantage of our method is that the auxiliary space can be chosen freely, to fit the class of operators, and a well-chosen space can give sharp constants, also on domains that are not convex, simply connected or bounded. On every intersection of two disks of the Riemann sphere, for operators with both closed disks as spectral sets, we obtain a complete bound independent of the two disks, which is sharp for the quantum annulus and the strip. For operators, bounded or m-sectorial, with numerical range in a sector, our bounds improve on the complete Crouzeix inequality for every opening; they are optimal for the right angle, answering a question of Crouzeix, and nearly optimal for acute angles. On Jordan domains with regular real-analytic boundary, a space built from the exterior conformal map and the Faber polynomials of the domain gives complete bounds for operators whose double-layer potential is bounded below. They are optimal for the disk, recover the complete Crouzeix inequality on convex domains, and improve on earlier bounds, including bounds of Crouzeix and Greenbaum, also on nonconvex domains.
item.dc:creator: Mihai Putinar, Georgios Tsikalas

item.title: Asymptotic delta-like behavior of the weighted taper in Thomson's multitaper F-test
item.description: arXiv:2611.01941v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the weighted taper arising in Thomson's multitaper F test, which is constructed from pre-plunge discrete prolate spheroidal wave functions (DPSWF). Numerical evidence suggests that, in the asymptotic regime, the Fourier transform of this taper converges to a delta measure supported at the origin. We provide a rigorous theoretical justification for this behavior.
item.dc:creator: Hau-Tieng Wu

item.title: Fundamental solutions to Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck equations with unbounded lower order terms
item.description: arXiv:2611.02886v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We continue the study of fundamental solutions for equations involving Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck operators with rough local or non-local diffusions. Here we consider possibly unbounded lower order terms, such as drifts and potentials. We prove existence and uniqueness of weak solutions and of an appropriate notion of fundamental solution for a wide class of kinetic equations. This is based on kinetic transfer of regularity and anisotropic embeddings.
item.dc:creator: Pascal Auscher (LMO)

item.title: Counterexamples to the Jacobian Conjecture from the viewpoint of lineability
item.description: arXiv:2611.03572v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Algebraic genericity in the family of polynomial counterexamples to the recently solved Jacobian Conjecture for $N\ge3$ is investigated. The notion of affine-coneability is introduced and it is shown that this family is affine-coneable and 1-lineable, but not 2-lineable. Semigroupability is further studied with respect to coordinatewise multiplication and composition.
item.dc:creator: L. Bernal-Gonz\'alez, M. C. Calder\'on-Moreno, J. A. Prado-Bassas

item.title: $q$-Bernstein functions and applications
item.description: arXiv:1602.02956v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterize q-Bernstein functions by exponential tests and, on a geometric lattice, by a well-defined spectral q-Laplace convolution semigroup. We also establish results on q-completely monotonic, q-log-completely monotonic, and q-Bernstein functions and give applications to q-gamma functions.
item.dc:creator: Valmir Krasniqi, Toufik Mansour

item.title: Invariant Flags for Singularly Perturbed Logarithmic Systems of Rank Two
item.description: arXiv:1909.04011v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study rank-two differential systems $\hbar x \partial_x \psi + A (x, \hbar) \psi = 0$ near a logarithmic pole, with coefficients that are holomorphic in $x$ and admit uniform factorial asymptotic expansions in the complex parameter $\hbar$. If the classical residue has distinct eigenvalues, then upon choosing an ordering and an admissible $\hbar$ direction, we transform this system to an upper-triangular form by a holomorphic gauge transformation with the same factorial asymptotic regularity on a sector in the $\hbar$-plane. Its diagonal is fully determined by the $\hbar \to 0$ and $x \to 0$ limits. This construction produces a canonical $(x,\hbar)$-dependent invariant flag. This flag specialises to the usual Levelt filtration for nonzero values of $\hbar$ on a narrower sector, and its associated graded converges to the eigenspaces of the residue as $x \to 0$ and of the leading-order matrix as $\hbar \to 0$. A Schr\"odinger example gives a uniform matching formula between the WKB data and the exact Frobenius exponent at a double pole.
item.dc:creator: Nikita Nikolaev

item.title: Expressing a difference between two Hurwitz zeta functions in terms of the Gauss hypergeometric functions
item.description: arXiv:2502.00624v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the paper, the author expresses the difference $2^m[\zeta(-m,\lambda z)-\zeta(-m,\lambda z+\mu)]$ for $m\in\mathbb{N}_0$ and $\Re(z)>0$ with $\lambda,\mu>0$ in terms of the functions $\Gamma(j+1){\,}_2F_1(-j,-z;1;2)$ for $0\le j\le m$ and $z\in\mathbb{C}$ in the form of matrix equations, where $\Gamma(z)$, $\zeta(z,\alpha)$, and ${}_2F_1(a,b;c;z)$ stand for the classical Euler gamma function, the Hurwitz zeta function, and the Gauss hypergeometric function, respectively. The case of non-integer $t$ in $2^t[\zeta(-t,\lambda z)-\zeta(-t,\lambda z+\mu)]$ is left open. The coefficients are characterized by matrix formulas and by an explicit recursion; closed-form expressions for them are not obtained. This problem originates from the Landau level quantization in solid state materials.
item.dc:creator: Feng Qi

item.title: Midpoints and critical points
item.description: arXiv:2512.07322v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a degree $5$ real polynomial with roots $x_1\leq \cdots \leq x_5$ and roots $\xi_1\leq \cdots \leq \xi_4$ of its derivative, we set $z_j:=(x_j+x_{j+1})/2$, $1\leq j\leq 4$. We prove that one cannot have at the same time $\min_{1\leq j\leq 3}(z_{j+1}-z_j)\geq \min_{1\leq j\leq 3}(\xi_{j+1}-\xi_j)$ and $\max_{1\leq j\leq 3}(z_{j+1}-z_j)\geq \max_{1\leq j\leq 3}(\xi_{j+1}-\xi_j)$. The result settles a general question about midpoints and critical points of hyperbolic polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Yousra Gati, Vladimir Petrov Kostov

item.title: Dunkl--BMO functions representable in terms of generalized balayage of Carleson measures and an application
item.dc:creator: Qingdong Guo

item.title: Improved dimension bounds for Falconer's distance problem in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.05500v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $E\subset\mathbb R^2$ be analytic with $t=\dim_{\mathrm H}E>1$. We prove $\dim_{\mathrm H}\Delta E\ge 4/5+\eta_0$ for an absolute, non-explicit constant $\eta_0>0$, and \[ \dim_{\mathrm H}\Delta E\ge \frac{t^2-2t+5}{2t^2-7t+10} \quad\text{for }1<t\le\frac{11-\sqrt{41}}{4}, \] which reaches $7/8$ at the right endpoint. For pinned distances, $\dim_{\mathrm H}\Delta_xE\ge q_*=0.7813\ldots$ for every $x\in\mathbb R^2$ outside an exceptional set of Hausdorff dimension at most one, with stronger bounds depending on $t$ and further exceptional-set estimates. If $E$ is compact and supports an $s$-Frostman measure $\mu$, $s>1$, then \[ \underline{\dim}_{\mathrm B}\Delta_xE\ge \max\left\{\frac45+\eta_0,\min\left\{\frac{3s+1}{5},\frac78\right\}\right\} \] for $\mu$-almost every $x$. The same bound holds for pinned Hausdorff dimension under a common dyadic mass law, allowing oscillation with scale. We retain information about both endpoints in the Kolmogorov complexity estimates of Stull and Fiedler--Stull. Applying the partition estimates with the endpoints reversed yields $4/5$ and the rational bound. Equality forces both information profiles to have excess information on a common interval of scales. Encoding one source measure for all pins converts this constraint into a configuration of points and circles with many rich perpendicular bisectors. Lower bounds of Katz--Tardos and Ren--Wang contradict the upper bound of Fu--Gan--Ren; compactness then gives $\eta_0>0$. This rigidity argument has a precedent in the work of H\'era, Shmerkin and Yavicoli on Furstenberg sets, using Bourgain's projection theorem. A separate finite-scale selection proves the pinned lower box bound.
item.dc:creator: Alex Iosevich, Alexia Yavicoli

item.title: Positive Bidiagonal Factorizations and Mixed-Type Chebyshev Multiple Orthogonal Polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.08568v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We characterize when a semi-infinite banded totally positive matrix admits a positive bidiagonal factorization, without assuming boundedness, and establish criteria for stability under perturbations. These criteria distinguish whether the initial factor entries are fixed or allowed to vary. For banded totally positive Toeplitz matrices, such factorizations always exist; a factorization can be chosen to depend analytically on all sufficiently small perturbations within the same band if and only if the polynomial symbol has distinct roots. Explicit root formulas determine the associated mixed-type multiple orthogonal polynomials and their matrix of positive measures. They also yield scalar linear forms independent of the chosen factorization, from which we obtain asymptotic zero spacing and sine-kernel limits. We further treat finite boundary modifications and limiting zero distributions for matrices with convergent diagonals.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Ma\~nas

item.title: Uniformly Bounded Orthonormal Bases of Homogeneous Polynomials on the Complex Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.14160v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We resolve the long-standing problem of Rudin concerning uniformly bounded orthonormal bases of homogeneous polynomials on complex unit spheres. Specifically, we show that for every $K \geq 2$ and $N \geq 0$ there exists a basis of degree $N$ homogeneous polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^K$ that is orthonormal with respect to the surface measure of the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^K$ and uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on $K$ on the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^K$. Bourgain resolved the case $K = 2$ in 1985 and the case $K = 3$ in 2016. No cases $K \geq 4$ were previously known.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Gon\c{c}alves, Jo\~ao P. Ferreira, Maksym Radziwi\l{}\l{}

item.title: Cone Restriction Estimates under Half-Scale Dimensional Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.16294v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study weighted Fourier extension estimates for the truncated cone. Building on the framework of Du--Li--Wang--Zhang, we introduce a more refined trilinear estimate. We obtain this estimate by applying weighted bilinear restriction on half-scale cubes and combining tube traversal with trilinear Kakeya to sum the local packet energies. Together with Lorentz rescaling, it yields improved weighted extension estimates.
item.dc:creator: Xiangyu Wang

item.title: A Criterion for Finite Hypergeometric Reductions of Lauricella's $F_C$ with Arguments Related by Cube Roots of Unity
item.description: arXiv:2610.22933v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the germ at the origin of Lauricella's function $F_C^{(3)}(a,b;c_0,c_1,c_2;\kappa,\omega\kappa,\omega^2\kappa)$, where $\omega=\exp(2\pi\sqrt{-1}/3)$. We assume that $a,b,c_0,c_1,c_2$ avoid nonpositive integers and that $c_0,c_1,c_2$ also avoid half-integers. We consider finite linear combinations of ordinary generalized hypergeometric series with arguments $\alpha\kappa^3$, where $\alpha$ is a nonzero complex constant that may vary between summands, each multiplied by a nonnegative integer power of $\kappa$. Every target series has lower parameters outside the nonpositive integers and converges near the origin or terminates. We prove that such a representation exists if and only if, for each $j=0,1,2$, either $c_j-c_0$ or $c_j+c_0$ is an integer, and construct finite sums of ordinary ${}_9F_8$ functions when this condition holds. We prove necessity from irreducible differential equations of order $24$ for the generating functions of the three coefficient subsequences and from their formal solutions at infinity.
item.dc:creator: Ryunosuke Nakano

item.title: Sharp Variational estimates for Schr\"{o}dinger equation in $\mathbb{R}^{2}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.31099v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For $p\geq2$ and $r\geq 1$, we prove the sharp strong $r$-variation estimate for solutions to the free Schr\"odinger equation $$ \bigl\|V^r_{[0,1]}\{e^{it\Delta}f\}\bigr\|_{L^p(\mathbb R^2)} \lesssim \|f\|_{H^s(\mathbb R^2)}. $$ The estimate holds if $s> s(p,r)$ and fails if $s< s(p,r)$, where $$s(p,r)=\max\left\{ \frac{2}{r}+\frac{1}{p}-\frac12,\, \frac{2}{r}-\frac{2}{p},\, \frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{r},\, \frac{2}{p}-\frac13,\, 1-\frac{2}{p} \right\}.$$ In particular, $s(3,\infty)=1/3$. Thus our result yields a sharp variational extension of the two-dimensional Schr\"odinger maximal estimate of Du, Guth, and Li [{Ann. Math.}, 186, 607--640 (2017)]. The proof employs fractal restriction estimates to eliminate the regularity loss originating from the summation in the variation norm.
item.dc:creator: Yanping Chen, Yongrui Tang

item.title: Minor summation formula of hyperpfaffians and Selberg integrals
item.description: arXiv:2008.09776v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In the previous paper (J. Combin. Theory Ser. A, 120, 2013, 1263--1284) H. Tagawa and the two authors proposed an algebraic method to compute certain Pfaffians whose form resemble to Hankel determinants associated with moment sequences of the classical orthogonal polynomials. At the end of the paper they offered several conjectures. In this work we employ a completely different method to evaluate this type of Pfaffians. The idea is to apply certain de Bruijn type formula and convert the evaluation of the Pfaffians to the certain Selberg type integrals. This approach works not only for Pfaffians but also for hyperpfaffians. Hence it enables us to establish much more generalized identities than those conjectured in the previous paper. We also investigate some Pfaffians related to classical $q$-orthogonal polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Masao Ishikawa, Jiang Zeng

item.title: Veronese sections and interlacing matrices of polynomials and formal power series
item.description: arXiv:2404.12989v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The concept of a fully interlacing matrix of formal power series with real coefficients is introduced. This concept extends and strengthens that of an interlacing sequence of real-rooted polynomials with nonnegative coefficients, in the special case of row and column matrices. The fully interlacing property is shown to be preserved under matrix products, flips across the reverse diagonal and Veronese sections of the power series involved. These results and their corollaries generalize, unify and simplify several results which have previously appeared in the literature. An application to the theory of uniform triangulations of simplicial complexes is included.
item.dc:creator: Christos A. Athanasiadis, David G. Wagner

item.title: Atomic decomposition of Bergman-Orlicz space on the upper complex half-plane
item.description: arXiv:2503.23570v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this work, we propose an atomic decomposition of the Bergman-Orlicz spaces on the complex upper half-plane. Using this result, we characterize Carleson embeddings with loss between Bergman-Orlicz spaces and certain Orlicz spaces. We also leverage this last result to control the composition operator between two Bergman-Orlicz spaces.
item.dc:creator: J. M. Tanoh Dje, Beno\^it. F. Sehba

item.title: A family of nonlocal energies whose minimizers are supported on two intervals
item.description: arXiv:2510.11662v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we consider the one-dimensional interaction energy $\frac{1}{2}\int_{\mathbb{R}}(W*\rho)(x)d\rho(x) + \int_{\mathbb{R}}U(x)d\rho(x)$ where the interaction potential $W(x)= -\frac{|x|^b}{b},\,1\le b \le 2$ and the external potential $U(x)=\frac{|x|^4}{4}$, and $\rho$ is a compactly supported probability measure on the real line. Our main result shows that the minimizer is supported on two intervals when $1<b<2$, showing in particular how the support of the minimizer transits from an interval (when $b=1$) to two points (when $b=2$) as $b$ increases. As a crucial part of the proof, we develop a new version of the iterated balayage algorithm, the original version of which was designed by Benko, Damelin, Dragnev and Kuijlaars for logarithmic potentials in one dimension. We expect the methodology in this paper can be generalized to study minimizers of interaction energies in $\mathbb{R}^d$ whose support is possibly an annulus.
item.dc:creator: Steven B. Damelin, Ruiwen Shu

item.title: On the dimension drop for harmonic measure on uniformly non-flat Ahlfors-David regular boundaries
item.description: arXiv:2601.16167v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We extend earlier results of Azzam on the dimension drop of the harmonic measure for a domain $\Omega\subset \R^{n}$ with $n\geq 3$, with dimensional Ahlfors regular boundary $\partial\Omega$ of dimension $s$ with $n-1-\delta_0 \leq s\leq n-1$, that is uniformly non flat. Here $\delta_0$ is a small positive constant dependent on the parameters of the problem. Our novel construction relies on elementary geometric and potential theoretic considerations. We avoid the use of Riesz transforms and compactness arguments, and also give quantitative bounds on the $\delta_0$ parameter.
item.dc:creator: Aritro Pathak

item.title: Cumulative angular cancellation in Maz'ya's endpoint inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2609.12755v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We establish domain criteria for critical homogeneous potential inequalities in the plane. Assuming signed plane cancellation, uniform absolute summability of frozen annular moments at each boundary centre implies the nonlinear endpoint estimate on arbitrary bounded open sets. For the Newton kernel and trace-free quadratic integrands, uniform boundedness of signed cumulative moments over all source centres and truncation radii is necessary and sufficient; testing all translates and dilates of one fixed radial unit-mass mollifier suffices. Tangent-cone cancellation on finitely cornered Dini domains follows as a geometric corollary. On one explicit strictly convex, non-Dini $C^1$ domain, the estimate holds for $2\xi_1\xi_2$ and fails for $\xi_1^2-\xi_2^2$ with $\log\log(1/\varepsilon)$ divergence. A Laplacian-measure extension transfers density estimates to PDE inequalities on the Dini class and on strictly convex $C^1$ domains. We also classify quadratic cancellation on polygons. The signed necessary-and-sufficient criterion is restricted to quadratic integrands.
item.dc:creator: Zhouyu Long, Wenming Zou

item.title: Reasonable bounds for Restricted Polynomial Progressions in $\mathbb F^n_p$
item.dc:creator: Alex Burgin, Anastasios Fragkos, David Kruzel, Michael Lacey, Amelia Stokolosa

item.title: Sharp Bounds for Nodal Sets of Steklov Eigenfunctions on Smooth Surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.28391v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a sharp linear upper bound for the interior nodal length of Steklov eigenfunctions on smooth compact Riemannian surfaces with boundary, establishing the upper bound predicted by the Steklov analogue of Yau's conjecture in dimension two. On each fixed surface, we also show that the nodal length divided by the logarithm of the eigenvalue tends to infinity, uniformly over the eigenfunctions. We construct examples to show this divergence can be arbitrarily slow. These examples rule out every general lower bound by a positive power of the eigenvalue, in contrast with the linear lower bound on analytic surfaces by Polterovich-Sher-Toth. Moreover, boundary zero counts and both interior and boundary nodal domain counts satisfy sharp linear bounds for large eigenvalues. We also prove density estimates for boundary zeros on at least one boundary component and construct a fixed analytic cylinder on which another component remains free of boundary zeros along an unbounded sequence of eigenvalues.
item.dc:creator: Guiyu Xie, Cheng Zhang
